comment: Each shot names the elements clicked to reach it, in order, one per frame.
They are element ids in the exported menu.rml, clicked through the bridge's
own listeners — the same path a player's pointer takes. An id that is not
in the document stops the run rather than screenshotting the wrong screen.
A slider has no click, so id@fraction sets it: volume-level@0.15 is the
slider fifteen percent of the way across.
A step written "wait:120" waits that many frames instead, which is how
anything on a clock is photographed at a chosen moment.
A shot that needs a different game says so beside its script: what is drawn
over a running game does not exist in an export that opens at the menu,
because the player is already looking at the menu. The window is never
focused here. The launcher sees ROMINABOX_MENU_SHOT and keeps the console
moving for that run, without writing the player's controls.cfg.
These are the same states scripts/fixtures/menu-states.json declares, but
reached rather than posed: menu-states sets the classes itself, and cannot
show that pressing CONTROLS gets you to the controls screen.
The achievement shots need --achievements <dir> containing achievements.json and badges/.
The rewrite baseline stages the original menu-achievements.json fixture and generated badges, without using the service.
